notes: Delete of a derived fact (as replace-0003): the premises would re-derive it, so each world forgets one premise (gives_up). 'Pixar's parent company' is its immediate owner, direct_subsidiary_of (since 2026-10-31, as replace-0003). q1 ('the same US state as Pixar itself') is a join: the parent's headquarters city lies in a state that contains Pixar's headquarters city. Pixar in Emeryville, California is q1's bridge, and 'a city lies in one US state' is firm, stated per named city as a class axiom with a nominal (located_in is transitive, so it can't be functional, and a rule would not fire on the join's unnamed state). Relabelled dl on 2026-10-31 (COVERAGE.md label corrections); the fol section keeps its Z3 encoding as a second check.

queries.ask: pixar : parent_headquartered_in some (located_in some (USState and inv(located_in) some (inv(headquartered_in) value pixar)))

fol.notes: One uninterpreted sort. headquartered_in and parent_headquartered_in are functions (RELATIONS.md: functional); the parent rule is the firm definitional premise, as in the DL file. 'Same US state' needs a place to be in one US state (firm) and California and New York to be distinct. Pixar's own headquarters (Emeryville, California) is a firm bridge: it moves in neither world. Delete of a derived fact: each world forgets one premise, so the parent's headquarters (and its state) is left open.

pixar_disney.says: Pixar is owned by the Walt Disney Company. (premise)

disney_burbank.says: The Walt Disney Company is headquartered in Burbank. (premise)

parent_rule.says: A company's parent company is the company that owns it: its parent's headquarters city is that owner's.
parent_rule.z3: ForAll([a, p], Implies(direct_subsidiary_of(a, p), parent_headquartered_in(a) == headquartered_in(p)))

pixar_emeryville.says: Pixar is headquartered in Emeryville, California. (stored)

one_state.says: A place is in one US state.
one_state.z3: ForAll([x, s, t], Implies(And(us_state(s), us_state(t), located_in(x, s), located_in(x, t)), s == t))
